blokken: AI advice that helps you decide
Practical insights for better AI decisions.
Real-world experience, frameworks and no-nonsense advice for senior leaders who want to put AI to work with impact. 12 articles, none of them written to sell you anything.
Book a call → See my case studies → 30 min., no pitch deck

Independent AI consultant vs agency vs Big 4
A fair comparison on independence, speed, depth, cost and delivery power, so you choose the right partner, even when that isn't me.
AI agents: what they can and cannot do in a business process
Agents that carry out tasks independently are the promise of the moment. Where they work, where they break down, and the question you need to answer first.
From AI strategy to value: a 3-step plan
Most AI strategies don't fail on the strategy itself, but on translating it. Three steps that force that translation.
Build, buy or partner: what fits your situation?
The question is rarely "can we build this ourselves?" but "do we still want to be maintaining this in three years?" A decision framework in four questions.
Which AI use cases actually deliver results?
Not the most spectacular, but the most boring. Four traits the winners share, and four patterns that almost always stall.
Independent AI consultant vs agency vs Big 4
A fair comparison on independence, speed, depth, cost and delivery power, so you choose the right partner, even when that isn't me.
The role of the data foundation in successful AI initiatives
"Get your data in order first" is as often an excuse as it is a necessity. How to work out which one applies to you.
AI governance without bureaucracy: what you need at minimum
Governance nobody uses protects nobody. Four mechanisms that make the difference, and what you can safely skip.
Why AI pilots stall (and what to do about it)
The pilot worked. Everyone was excited. And a year later, nothing has scaled up. Five causes, five countermeasures.
The business case for AI: how to calculate it honestly
Time saved isn't a saving until someone spends that time differently. A costing model that survives the CFO's scrutiny.
AI adoption starts with the work, not the tool
Giving everyone a licence isn't an adoption strategy. Why an empty input box is the biggest barrier, and what actually works.
AI vendor selection in eight steps
Criteria first, vendors second. A selection process built to withstand good demos and internal preferences.
When do you really need an AI strategist?
Half the time, the answer is: you don't. Four situations where outside help pays off, and four where you're better off doing it yourself.
